name: SPARC line, version N
data: 175 SPARC galaxies against version N: the a0 law's sector kept apart from a cold dark energy halo whose core comes from native zooms, with η measured at ng 80 at 10¹⁰, 10¹¹ and 10¹² solar masses, nine seeds each. One Υ per galaxy; the line is median Υ in 0.50–0.80 and rms at most 0.110, on both backgrounds.
picture: Left: median Υ in each V_flat bin with the frozen window shaded; the window grades the sample median, not each bin. Right: the sample median Υ for each of 40 draws that resample all three η medians together, green on the line, red off it.
why: The lane's own label is ALL-NG80 PASSES [NOISE-LIMITED], and this dish does not print it as a pass. Seed noise alone takes the median off the line: 16 of 40 draws land above 0.80, none below 0.50, and 40 draws is a coarse estimate of seed scatter only. The median also hides a run of Υ with V_flat, from 1.20 in dwarfs (the top of the Υ grid) to 0.57 at 150–200 km/s, so the tilt reads +0.59 against the 0.15 line. The same runs fail cluster keys G-IN-all, G-MID-T3 and G-IN-Mall, all over.

numbers.what: Υ A / B, rms A / B
draws on the line; high; low

name: Groups, version N
data: 63 galaxy groups: measured velocity dispersion against the dispersion version N predicts. Mean difference +0.062 dex, total error 0.042 dex.
picture: A Z scale with |Z| ≤ 2 shaded. The large green dot is version N; below it the same groups under the same machinery with other mass rules, for scale.
why: Version N's mean sits +1.47 error bars from the measurement, inside the line, and adding the response barely moves it (+1.50). It reads +1.47 at every input in NR2's band, because the groups don't depend on the low-mass η. The pass belongs to EM1's mass line: the fair-share mass rows read +3.75 and +5.30, NOT DIAGNOSTIC. Groups are one gate of several, in a lane whose overall label answers a different question.

name: Cluster keys on measured gas
data: Fifteen stacked weak-lensing keys on eRASS1 clusters against the native z = 0 profile at ng 80 (six seeds at each of 10¹⁴ and 10¹⁵), with gas masses on the measured scale. GS4 measured that scale on 45 clusters against published Chandra and XMM gas masses.
picture: Left: Z for each key, filled on the measured gas (+0.005), hollow on +0.111, with |Z| ≤ 2 shaded. Right: the gas offset itself, GS4's measurement with its error, the +0.093 the pass needs, and the +0.111 from five massive clusters.
why: On the gas that was measured, G-MID-T3, G-OUT-Mall, G-OUT-M3 go over 2. ZN4's frozen verdict was CONVERGED and its class graded on +0.111 only, where 15 of 15 keys pass; that is a statement about resolution, and the measured +0.005 ± 0.017 is over 5 standard errors below the needed offset. The hollow points are shown as a scale the data don't support, not as a result. This is the native profile's path; version N's own path also has 12 of 15, with other keys (G-IN-Mall, G-IN-all, G-MID-T3) failing, and the two aren't comparable.

name: X-COP, two profiles
data: Seven X-COP clusters, 35 rows at x ≤ 0.75: hydrostatic mass against baryons plus model mass. One row of results for the native z = 0 profile at ng 80, one for version N's path.
picture: Left: mean residual in each x bin for both paths. Right: the two paths in the mean and rms plane, with the frozen box |mean| ≤ 0.05, rms ≤ 0.10 shaded.
why: These are different profiles, so the two rows are not an improvement of one over the other and shouldn't be read as a trend. The native profile lands inside the box at +0.013, 0.075, but the gate is built from hydrostatic masses and RF3 found no clean hydrostatic-free X-COP mass on disk, so without them this is UNDETERMINED. Version N's path misses at -0.160, 0.186. Hence conditional: the pass belongs to one path and rests on one kind of mass. Native reads the same at either gas scale because X-COP's line uses its own gas.

name: LITTLE THINGS, version N
data: LITTLE THINGS dwarfs against version N with no response, on both backgrounds. Baryons are a point mass inside R_max, by hand, as stated in UR1's criteria.
picture: A scale of median E with |E| ≤ 0.10 shaded; one row per input, circle and square for the two backgrounds, red outside the line.
why: At NR2's median η version N's dwarfs read +0.153 / +0.147, outside the 0.10 line on both backgrounds. NR2's high band does read +0.093 / +0.085, but a band run reaching a line isn't a pass: that is NR2's upper band, ρ at p84. Adding the response at the median, +0.116 / +0.109, still fails.

name: Live contraction
data: A disc grown in a live zoom at 10¹² solar masses, nine same-seed pairs with and without the disc, Newtonian, gravity only, no feedback, one mass. Then SPARC's line with the response on, on version N's inputs.
picture: Left: the measured contraction Q with radius against the Blumenthal and Gnedin formulas, with the band where f_Q is read. Right: Υ by V_flat with no response, at the measured strength f 0.87, and at full Blumenthal.
why: LC1's frozen grade is a success of the test, STRONG and BLUMENTHAL HOLDS: the cold fluid contracts about as the formula says. This dish is red because of what that does to SPARC: EM1 + Blumenthal reads Υ 0.35 / 0.36, and at the map cell nearest the measured strength, f 0.87, 0.39 / 0.39, both off the 0.50 line. NR3's label is SIGN FLIP YES, AMPLITUDE FAILS [NOISE-LIMITED]. The 150–250 km/s bins sit at 0.30–0.39 whatever the low-mass η does, so low-mass η can't close it. Feedback isn't in this test, and it says what gravity alone does: that's the wall a mechanism would have to overcome.

name: The requirement map
data: A grid of 36 cells on SPARC, groups and LITTLE THINGS: m multiplies the low-mass η, f scales the response. Both are FITTED: this is a requirement map, never a rule.
picture: A heat map, m by f: each cell shows Υ (background A) and which gates it fails. Darker is more gates failed; the green cell clears the SPARC side. The dashed column is LC1's measured strength.
why: The label is NOT DECIDED because frozen checks K2 and K3 missed 1e-6, at 5.6e-06 and 2.6e-06, so grey is the right colour. Read as a map, the one clearing cell is no net response with η × 1.5, which needs η(10¹⁰), η(10¹¹) of 40.1 and 37.1, above every seed (36.1, 33.8). Audit note: the grid starts at m 1, so 'no m reaches 0.50 at f 0.87' holds only for m ≥ 1; NR3's LOW, about m 0.67 / 0.60 at f 1, reads Υ 0.51 / 0.52 and fails tilt and LITTLE THINGS there. One cell on a 6 by 6 grid isn't a measured region, and it doesn't address clusters.

name: The doors tried today
data: Five of the doors tried on 1 November, each graded on SPARC by its own frozen criteria, each read from its own result files. DR1 is a density term on the law, with no cold dark energy at all; the other four sit on version N's path. CP1 breaks the rule that a0 stays out of the cold sector, on purpose.
picture: Each door's sample median Υ against the 0.50 line and the window, with the lane's own label and tilt beside it. DR9 takes three rows, for its three normalisations of C. The dotted line is the contracted baseline, EM1 + Blumenthal.
why: Every door's primary row stays below 0.50 except DR9's. DR9's frozen rows read 0.37 with C from the measured channel, 0.70 with C FITTED (20.6 × that channel) and 0.73 at the ceiling C = 1, and every row on the line fails tilt (+0.33 / +0.39 at the fitted one) and LITTLE THINGS. Its label is FAILS AT ALL THREE, but its frozen mutation check missed, moving Υ exactly 0.02 against 'more than 0.02', and the replacement check was written after the rows were seen, so strictly that run is NOT DECIDED. CP1 is NOT DECIDED because K4 failed; inside it galaxies fail on Υ 0.43, while a report-only reading, R2, passes the galaxy block on canonical at 0.53 by counting the cold at weight χ²_clust, matches no source term and fails on alt at 0.45. The chip is red for the set: nothing here clears, and the two NOT DECIDED rows are labelled as that, not as fails.

name: The law on the same gates (comparison dish, not route E)
data: The plain a0 law with no halo and no cold dark energy, DR1's baseline row (c = 0): SPARC, X-COP and the 15 keys on gas +0.005, f★ 0.034. κ = ½ is FITTED. The two footings aren't pooled.
picture: Five small panels, each with the gate's window shaded: Υ, rms, tilt, X-COP's mean, and the worst heavy-cluster key, on the canonical (circle) and alt (square) footing.
why: This dish is here for reference only, so route E's dishes can be read against the same gates; it's a different theory path, not a result of route E, and nothing here says the data favour either. On the canonical footing the law's SPARC gates hold; on alt its Υ 0.44 falls under 0.50. Clusters fail on both: X-COP +0.467, 0.476, and 10 of 15 keys with G-OUT-M3 +4.76. Groups read Z +0.31.
